Listen to this article Share Tunji Olowolafe, the Chancellor of Ekiti State University (EKSU) has mobilised friends and associates towards raising funds for the N1 billion Palace project in Ikogosi-Ekiti, in Ekiti West Local Government Area of Ekiti State. Olowolafe, a medical doctor-turned-industrialist, made this known at the 2026 Ikogosi Day celebration held on Saturday where he served as Chairman and Chief Launcher of the Oba’s Palace project. The renowned entrepreneur disclosed that he shared the responsibility of serving as Chief Launcher with more than 30 friends and associates in Lagos and Abuja who equally admire the Governor Biodun Oyebanji leadership model and are passionate about Ekiti’s development. He disclosed that the fundraising initiative, undertaken in collaboration with his friends and associates, had already secured close to the entire one-billion-naira target for the palace project. He said the project should serve not only as a befitting abode for the traditional ruler but also as a centre for preserving Ikogosi’s traditions, history and cultural heritage. “Today’s Oba’s Palace Project gives us a powerful anchor. Its primary purpose is to uphold our revered traditional institution and unite this community. “As we build it, let us also design it to preserve and showcase Ikogosi’s heritage, so that visitors meet not merely a scenic resort, but a proud people with a rich story to tell,” he said. Read also: Soil Erosion: Major environmental hazards in Nigeria He described the transformation of the Ikogosi Warm Springs Tourist Centre as phenomenal, advocating sustained investment and strategic partnerships to position the community as a global tourism destination. Recounting his longstanding relationship with Ikogosi, Olowolafe described the community as a place close to his heart, recalling how his parents took him and his siblings to their hometown, Are-Ekiti, every Christmas, with a visit to Ikogosi always a compulsory stop before returning to Lagos. He applauded the remarkable transformation of the tourist centre, describing it as phenomenal when compared with its outlook several years ago. The academic attributed the development to purposeful leadership, noting that Governor Biodun Oyebanji’s administration had created the motivation and enabling environment for stakeholders to maximise development opportunities. In his remarks, Governor Biodun Oyebanji urged the community, his country home, to remain focused on the original purpose of the palace project, stressing that the initiative must not be diverted from its objective of providing a befitting edifice for the traditional institution. The governor commended Olowolafe for his central role in mobilising resources, explaining that he deliberately entrusted him with the responsibilities of Chairman and Chief Launcher because the initiative was community-driven and not a government project. According to Oyebanji, with the approach adopted, misconceptions and misleading narratives about the initiative would be prevented.
